## Proposed January 15 Deadline for H-1B Registration Intake

For the upcoming cap season, I propose setting January 15 as our internal intake deadline, with later requests handled case by case. This would give employers a clear timetable and give us more time to review information before the registration window opens. The goal is better service and a more manageable workload—not treating clients as late when we have never given them a date.

Last season, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients. Nine of those registrations came in during the final week of February, and Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened. Our current process is to send a questionnaire whenever an employer asks, with no set intake date. Much of the crunch is therefore something we can address through our own process. One HR contact said she would happily have sent everything in January if we had asked.

Earlier intake also gives us a better opportunity to catch problems. Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window opened; the passport had expired in October, and we caught it because Rosa checked the dates. Registration itself is relatively simple, but errors can have expensive consequences, including jeopardizing the validity of a selection. We should build time for those checks into the schedule rather than rely on last-minute review.

The proposed changes are straightforward:

- Send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire the week of December 7, clearly stating the January 15 intake deadline.
- Have Rosa own the intake tracker, with a clean six weeks after the deadline to chase gaps and coordinate corrections.
- Review requests received after January 15 case by case, based on capacity and the time available for proper review.

January 15 is realistic: HR teams are back from the holidays, budgets are set, and employers already budget for the $215-per-beneficiary registration fee in Q1. I’d like Marcus and me to agree on this approach Thursday so we can prepare the December letters and give clients a clear, consistent schedule from the outset.
